name: CA-51
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+10 district with a Democratic incumbent seeking reelection
Jacobs has raised $1.6M with no outside opposition spending
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
No polls or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Jacobs: a D+10 seat, incumbency, and a large fundraising edge over a little-known Republican challenger with no visible outside support. Markets price her near-certain to win, so the forecast stays at a Safe D margin of about 21 points.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing a much closer race, or a surge of outside spending for Cabrera, would be the first sign this is more competitive than priced.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sara Jacobs, the Democratic incumbent, advanced to the general election in a San Diego-area district that leans Democratic by about ten points. She has raised roughly $1.6 million and holds a clear financial advantage over Republican Ricardo Cabrera, who has reported minimal fundraising and draws no outside support. No outside groups are spending against her.

With no public polls and no expert ratings in the race, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money, all of which favor Jacobs. Prediction markets put her chances near 96 percent. The expected margin is about 21 points, consistent with a Safe D rating, though the absence of polling keeps confidence at medium.
